sentences.text: (Clause 31) AWARD 1.
This is a claim petition U/s 166 read with Section 140 ( old ) of the Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988, filed by petitioners.

The brief facts of the present case are that on 27.02.2017, at about 6.00 p.m, the deceased Smt Poonam Dagar W/O Sh Mukhtiar Singh Dagar alongwith her husband went to a Carpenter's shop at 40 Foota Road,
near Bijender's Office, Roshan Pura, Najafgarh, Delhi within the jurisdiction of P.S Chhawla, Delhi.

While they were talking to Car painter they both were hit by a crane bearing No. TN 21 AU 4459, when driver of the crane was reversing the crane at very high speed without looking at backside, in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result of which Smt Poonam Dagar (since deceased) and her husband received multiple injuries.
Both the injured were taken to Bensups Hospital Dwarka, New Delhi.
Later on Smt Poonam Dagar was removed to Venketshwar Hospital, Dwarka, New Delhi.
The Doctor of Venketshwar Hospital after minutely examined the deceased declared her as dead.

The Post mortem of deceased was conducted at RTRM Hospital,
Jaffarpur,New Delhi.
The present compensation case pertains to the death of deceased Poonam Dagar.

2. It is contended in the application that the accident in question took place, due to rash and negligent driving of Crane bearing No. TN 21 AU4459, being driven by Sh Varun Kumar , hence he has been MACT No. 1374/17 Mukhtiar Singh & Ors Vs Varma Kumar & Ors Page No. 7 of 17 impleaded as respondent No.1.

entities.text: Mukhtiar Singh & Ors Vs Varma Kumar & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The offending vehicle is owned by Munish Sharma, hence he is impleaded as respondent No.2.

Since the offending vehicle was insured with TATA AIG General Insurance Company,
hence company is impleaded as respondent No.3.

By the present case, the petitioners are claiming a sum of Rs. 20,00,000/ ( Twenty Lacs ) from respondents alongwith interest @ 12% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
3. The respondent no. 1 has not filed any reply/WS .
4. The respondent No.2 has filed his reply/W.S stating therein that accident took place due to the sole negligence of deceased.

He has deposed that he alongwith his wife were taken to Bensups Hospital Dwarka, New Delhi.

sentences.text: The Doctor of Venketshwar Hospital, after minutely examined her, declared her as dead.
10. PW 1 has been crossexamined by respondent No.2 as well as by the insurance company but nothing material could come out in his cross examination which could disbelief his testimony.

The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338/304A of IPC. .
11.
The fact that deceased has died in the accident is also supported by the post martem report Ex PW2/A.
After investigation, police has also indicted respondent no. 1 as an accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338/304A IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 1.
The respondent no.1 has facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.

Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a crane bearing No.TN 21 AU 4459 by respondent no. 1 thereby causing death of Smt Poonam Dagar.

12. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Poonam Dagar died in a vehicular accident due to rash and negligent driving of acrane bearing No.TN MACT No. 1374/17 Mukhtiar Singh & Ors Vs Varma Kumar & Ors Page No. 10 of 17 21 AU 4459 by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2:
Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom ?
Petitioner no. 1 is husband of deceased Poonam Dagar and petitioner no. 2 is the son of deceased/victim, as such LRs of victim.
They are entitled for compensation.
Now it has to be decided whether the petitioners can be considered as dependent upon the victim.
Admittedly, the victim was the wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioner No.2 Being mother she might have love and affection towards her children as well as her husband.

She ( Victim) may have sometime prepared food, washing cloths and other house hold works for them, if she could alive for some time these works could have been continued being done by her( victim) for the petitioners being house maker.
So, I considered the petitioners as dependent upon victim.
14. Now coming to the extent of compensation.
According to deposition of PW1 deceased was doing the work of Agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/ P.M.
But petitioners have not placed on record any documentary proof such has revenue record showing that the deceased had owned any land for cultivation.
Even otherwise Ld Counsel for the petitioners has conceded to the fact that no such document like Fard etc is placed on record.
The Counsel has also conceded that income of the victim, for the purpose of computation, has to be considered on the basis of Minimum Wages.

In the given MACT No. 1374/17 Mukhtiar Singh & Ors Vs Varma Kumar & Ors Page No. 11 of 17 circumstances, this Tribunal has left with no option but to assessed the income of deceased as per Mukhtiar Singh Dagar And Ors vs Varma Kumar on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29388487/
7 Minimum Wages Act.

sentences.text: This Tribunal while relying upon a case titled as Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Master Manmeet Singh & Ors MAC.APP. 590/2011 decided by our own Hon'bel High Court on 30.01.2012, where it was held that services rendered by a housewife cannot be counted; cooking, washing, ironing clothes and stitching clothes (in some cases) for the husband and children, teaching and guiding them and working as a nurse, whenever husband or children are sick, are some of the major activities of housewife.

entities.text: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Master Manmeet Singh & Ors MAC.APP. 590/2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She has no fixed hours of work, she is also in attendance to take care of each and every need of daily family work at the cost of her personal comfort and health.
Thus value of services rendered by such home maker should be taken as minimum wages of a nonmatriculate (in the absence of any evidence to the contrary).

The question with regard to the income of a non earning member/housewife has also been dealt with by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Lata Wadhwa & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors., Writ Petition (civil) 232 of 1991.

entities.text: Lata Wadhwa & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors., Writ Petition (civil) 232 of 1991

15. As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court there is no future addition in the monthly salary after the age of 60 years.

sentences.text: Admittedly as per the petition, the deceased Poonam Dagar was 62 years of age at the time of accident.
16. The deceased Poonam Dagar was having two LRs, hence deceased/victim is presumed to be spending 1/3rd of her income on her personal expenses.
And therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.7,176/ ( 10,764/ - 3,588/) per month.
17. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
The age of the deceased was 62 years old ( as per averment in the petition )
A multiplier of 07 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.

Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs.
6,02,784/ (7,176/ x 12 x 07. ).
So an amount of Rs. 6,02,800/ in lumpsum is allowed to petitioners as loss of dependency.

There is no cross examination on these bills.
Hence, seeing nature of injuries suffered by deceased, a lump sum amount of Rs. 69,000/ is granted to petitioner towards medical expenses.
19. Apart from amount mentioned above, petitioner no. 1 is also granted a sum of Rs.17,000/ for funeral expenses.

Now coming to the extent of liability.
It has already been held herein above that the deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
He is primarily liable to make payment.
However, the petitioner has made the respondent no.3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no.3 to pay the compensation.
21. The only submission of Ld Counsel for insurance company is that the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It is submitted that respondent No.1 was not possessing any valid D/L and was driving the offending vehicle without having any valid and effective route permit and fitness, at the time of accident.

In this regard R3 has examined a witness as R3W1 Ms Asmita Singh , who has proved the copy of charge sheet Ex R3W1/1 to show that respondent No.1 has also been charge sheeted for the offence U/S 3/181of M.V Act.

Copy of notice sent U/O 12 rule 8 CPC sent to the driver and owner is also placed on record vide Ex R3W1/2.

22. My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No.1:
Whether Poonam Dagar sustained fatal injuries and Mukhtiar Singh Dagar sustained grievous injury in a motor vehicle accident dt 27.02.2017 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle ( Crane) No.TN21 AU4459 being driven by respondent No.1 Varma Kumar, owned by respondent No.2 Munish Sharma and insured by Respondent 3 TATA AGI General Insurance Co Ltd ? . OPP 9.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is a claim petition U/s 166 read with Section 140 ( old ) of the Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988, filed by petitioners.
While they were talking to Car painter they both were hit by a crane bearing No. TN 21 AU 4459, when driver of the crane was reversing the crane at very high speed without looking at backside, in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result of which Smt Poonam Dagar (since deceased) and her husband received multiple injuries.
Both the injured were taken to Bensups Hospital Dwarka, New Delhi.
2. It is contended in the application that the accident in question took place, due to rash and negligent driving of Crane bearing No. TN 21 AU4459, being driven by Sh Varun Kumar , hence he has been MACT No. 1374/17 Mukhtiar Singh & Ors Vs Varma Kumar & Ors Page No. 7 of 17 impleaded as respondent No.1.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338/304A of IPC. .
11.
Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a crane bearing No.TN 21 AU 4459 by respondent no. 1 thereby causing death of Smt Poonam Dagar.
In the given MACT No. 1374/17 Mukhtiar Singh & Ors Vs Varma Kumar & Ors Page No. 11 of 17 circumstances, this Tribunal has left with no option but to assessed the income of deceased as per Mukhtiar Singh Dagar And Ors vs Varma Kumar on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29388487/
7 Minimum Wages Act.
This Tribunal while relying upon a case titled as Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Master Manmeet Singh & Ors MAC.APP. 590/2011 decided by our own Hon'bel High Court on 30.01.2012, where it was held that services rendered by a housewife cannot be counted; cooking, washing, ironing clothes and stitching clothes (in some cases) for the husband and children, teaching and guiding them and working as a nurse, whenever husband or children are sick, are some of the major activities of housewife.
The question with regard to the income of a non earning member/housewife has also been dealt with by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Lata Wadhwa & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors., Writ Petition (civil) 232 of 1991.
15. As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court there is no future addition in the monthly salary after the age of 60 years.
MACT No. 1374/17 Mukhtiar Singh & Ors Vs Varma Kumar & Ors Page No. 12 of 17
Admittedly as per the petition, the deceased Poonam Dagar was 62 years of age at the time of accident.
16. The deceased Poonam Dagar was having two LRs, hence deceased/victim is presumed to be spending 1/3rd of her income on her personal expenses.
And therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.7,176/ ( 10,764/ - 3,588/) per month.
17. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
The age of the deceased was 62 years old ( as per averment in the petition )
A multiplier of 07 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
However, the petitioner has made the respondent no.3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no.3 to pay the compensation.
So it is proved on record that respondent No.1 was not having any valid and effective licence and route permit of offending vehicle at the time of accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
12. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Poonam Dagar died in a vehicular accident due to rash and negligent driving of acrane bearing No.TN MACT No. 1374/17 Mukhtiar Singh & Ors Vs Varma Kumar & Ors Page No. 10 of 17 21 AU 4459 by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2:
Even otherwise Ld Counsel for the petitioners has conceded to the fact that no such document like Fard etc is placed on record.
The Counsel has also conceded that income of the victim, for the purpose of computation, has to be considered on the basis of Minimum Wages.

p.a for delayed payment.

Petitioner No.2 vide his statement given on 25.08.2023 has relinquish his share in the award amount in favour of his father, petitioner No.1.
